condition: Endoscopy antithrombotic management — warfarin continued for diagnostic OGD ± biopsy
summary: 74-year-old woman on warfarin for AF (INR 2.3) booked for diagnostic gastroscopy ± biopsy for PPI-refractory dyspepsia (low bleeding-risk procedure).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Booked for a camera test of the stomach — takes warfarin
inputs.hpi: Three months of upper abdominal discomfort and reflux not settling on omeprazole. No weight loss, dysphagia, vomiting or melaena. Booked for diagnostic gastroscopy ± biopsies. Atrial fibrillation on warfarin (target 2–3), no previous stroke, no valve disease.

exam.general: Well. Irregular pulse 76, BP 132/78, RR 14, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.5°C.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no mass.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: PPI-refractory dyspepsia — diagnostic OGD ± biopsy; on warfarin for AF
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Dyspepsia not responding to PPI, no alarm features. Diagnostic OGD ± biopsy (low bleeding-risk). AF on warfarin, INR 2.3 — continue warfarin.

mustInclude.note: Check the INR is within the therapeutic range in the week before.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No 'continue warfarin' for a low-risk diagnostic OGD; the procedure's bleeding risk is not an input to any rule.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Replace the anticoag_check prompt in clinical-inference.ts with a rule table keyed on drug, indication and procedure bleeding risk (ACCP 2022 / BSG-ESGE 2021): warfarin — stop 5 days before, INR the day before, bridge only for mechanical mitral valve / recent VTE or stroke; DOAC — interrupt by drug, CrCl and bleeding risk, no bridging, no routine coagulation test; low-risk endoscopy — continue. Do not fire it for prophylactic-dose LMWH.

mustExclude.note: Low-risk procedure: warfarin continued; bridging is both unnecessary and a bleeding risk.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: anticoag_check 'warfarin — bridge with LMWH' for a procedure where warfarin should simply continue.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Replace the anticoag_check prompt in clinical-inference.ts with a rule table keyed on drug, indication and procedure bleeding risk (ACCP 2022 / BSG-ESGE 2021): warfarin — stop 5 days before, INR the day before, bridge only for mechanical mitral valve / recent VTE or stroke; DOAC — interrupt by drug, CrCl and bleeding risk, no bridging, no routine coagulation test; low-risk endoscopy — continue. Do not fire it for prophylactic-dose LMWH.

mustExclude.note: Reversing a therapeutic INR for a diagnostic gastroscopy exposes the patient to thromboembolism for no benefit.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The coagulopathy prompt fires on any INR >1.5 (here 2.3, therapeutic): 'Hold elective surgery until INR < 1.5' and 'PO Vitamin K 1–2mg — slow INR correction'. It ignores that the INR is an intended warfarin effect before a low-risk procedure. The negated HPI ('No weight loss, dysphagia, vomiting or melaena') also makes triage emergency_now.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Coagulopathy prompt: when the patient is on warfarin, compare INR with the target range and the planned procedure's bleeding risk; suggest reversal only for bleeding or urgent high-risk surgery.

guideline.name: BSG/ESGE guideline — endoscopy in patients on antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy (2021 update)
guideline.section: Low-risk procedures (diagnostic ± biopsy): continue P2Y12 inhibitors and warfarin (INR in the week before, within therapeutic range), omit the morning DOAC dose. High-risk procedures (polypectomy, EMR, ERCP with sphincterotomy): P2Y12 inhibitor stopped 7 days before when thrombotic risk is low; high thrombotic risk (coronary stents) — continue aspirin and liaise with the cardiologist about stopping the P2Y12 inhibitor; warfarin stopped 5 days before (INR <1.5), bridging only for high thrombotic risk; DOAC stopped before the procedure (interval by drug and renal function), no bridging
guideline.citation: Veitch AM, Radaelli F, Alikhan R, et al. Gut. 2021;70:1611–28.

guideline.name: BRIDGE trial — perioperative bridging anticoagulation in AF
guideline.section: Forgoing bridging was non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism and reduced major bleeding in patients with AF interrupting warfarin
guideline.citation: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Kaatz S, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:823–33.

rationale: Permutation: low bleeding-risk procedure on warfarin. The right answer is to continue warfarin (INR within range). Tests over-management: bridging, reversal or deferral.
